sections.title: 1. Registro de campo y localización de muestras

steps.action: Abra Recepción (/reception). Use el lector de código de barras o búsqueda para localizar la muestra pre-registrada desde KoBo.
steps.expected: La muestra se muestra con estado EXPECTED. Escanear localiza un registro y sincronizar importa datos; ninguno por sí solo constituye recepción física.

sections.title: 2. Inspección física y verificación de condición

steps.action: Examine el recipiente físico, coincidencia de etiqueta, sello, humedad y peso. Registre cualquier daño, derrame o cantidad insuficiente.
steps.expected: Las no conformidades se documentan. Las no conformidades graves se pueden poner en cuarentena o rechazar (RECEIVED_REJECTED).

steps.action: Asigne o verifique el ID de laboratorio único (labId) y haga clic en Confirmar recepción.
steps.expected: La recepción oficial establece receptionDate con la fecha actual y avanza el estado a RECEIVED/ACCEPTED. Las tareas de secado y preparación se desbloquean en los bancos de trabajo (/workbench). Los contadores del panel (Recibidas hoy) se actualizan en base a receptionDate.

steps: Abra Recepción (/reception). Use el lector de código de barras o búsqueda para localizar la muestra pre-registrada desde KoBo. (Esperado: La muestra se muestra con estado EXPECTED. Escanear localiza y sincronizar importa; ninguno constituye recepción física.)
Examine el recipiente físico, coincidencia de etiqueta, sello, humedad y peso. (Esperado: Las no conformidades se documentan; las graves se rechazan como RECEIVED_REJECTED.)

Asigne o verifique el ID de laboratorio único (labId) y haga clic en Confirmar recepción. (Esperado: La recepción oficial establece receptionDate y pasa a RECEIVED/ACCEPTED. Se desbloquean tareas de secado y preparación.)

articles.summary: Sigue Identificación y campo, Condición, Análisis y Entrega usando una muestra sintética de proyecto.
articles.quick: Compara la etiqueta con el registro esperado del proyecto, registra la masa y excepciones de condición, verifica los análisis solicitados y confirma la recepción.
before: Have the physical material, label, delivery information and required intake measurements available.
Confirm your laboratory and project scope. Use the existing project record when one already represents the sample.
The exact final receipt control and any manager intake review depend on the deployed workflow; the writer must bind and verify those controls before publication.

steps.action: Open Reception and select the project. In ID & Field, find or scan the identifier on the physical label.
steps.expected: A matching source record is displayed. A KoBo submission is field provenance, not proof that the material arrived.

steps.action: Compare project, field identifier and displayed laboratory identifier. Check the source location and sampling information.
steps.expected: The correct project record is linked. If source coordinates exist but the draft is blank, preserve the discrepancy instead of inventing coordinates.

steps.action: Open Condition. Enter the actual received mass in the stated unit, the observed condition and the required compliance answers.
steps.expected: Missing values, insufficient mass or nonconformance are visible as specific issues rather than silently accepted defaults.

steps.action: Document any required exception reason. In Analyses, review the parameter names and method choices against the request.
steps.expected: The ordered work matches the request. Grouped analyses such as texture are handled according to the configured panel, not invented as unrelated tasks.

steps.action: Open Handover and review identity, condition, ordered analyses and outstanding issues. Use Save draft if the entry is not ready.
steps.expected: A saved draft remains distinct from an accepted receipt; it should not move unreceived material into drying workload.

steps.action: When complete, perform the verified final receipt action and inspect its confirmation and resulting intake state.
steps.expected: The application identifies what was received and whether another intake-review action remains. Final control binding is a required publication check for this exemplar.

steps.action: Check the sample label and the destination or handover details before transferring the physical material.
steps.expected: The next worker can identify the material and locate the corresponding tasks without duplicating intake.

sections.title: 1. Select the work and prepare the data

steps.action: Open Workbench and choose the required analysis method in Worksheet. Compare the displayed parameter and method with your bench record.

steps.action: For a spreadsheet paste, prepare two columns: Sample ID and Result Value. Copy the data rows, without column headings. Keep identifiers as text so leading zeros are not lost.

steps.action: Compare the included identifiers and values with the source record. Resolve errors at their cause. If 38 of 40 rows match, do not describe the import as 40 completed results.

steps.action: Select Apply 38 Matched Drafts, or the actual displayed count. Check the worksheet values and required instrument, units or basis metadata.

steps.action: Select the intended worksheet rows and choose Review Completion. Inspect Included Determinations and Excluded / Incomplete.

steps.action: Read the confirmation, select it only after checking the entries, and choose Record N Determinations.

steps.action: Open Ready to Submit. Inspect each selected sample's included analyses and whether the submission is FULL or PARTIAL.

steps.action: Open Sent & Completed and verify the submitted work or receipt. If the manager cannot find it, provide that receipt and check the laboratory and queue filters before repeating anything.

sections.title: 1. Reconnect without losing the local record

steps.action: Restore a stable connection and confirm the signed-in account and laboratory.
steps.expected: The queued work is reconciled under the correct identity; another lab's cache is not used.

steps.action: Open the actual synchronization status or pending-work view supplied by the application.
steps.expected: You can distinguish queued actions from completed server operations and see the recorded failure reasons.

steps.action: Inspect each completed action and its server confirmation. For a partial sync, compare the number and identities of completed and still-pending actions.
steps.expected: A global online indicator is not mistaken for successful submission of every result or attachment.

steps.action: For a retryable transport failure, use the application's retry/reconciliation action after checking whether the server already recorded it.
steps.expected: The original operation identity is preserved; an uncertain response does not produce a duplicate result.

steps.action: For a conflict, compare the local entry and current server state and follow the permitted resolution. If work was reassigned or approved, involve the responsible manager.
steps.expected: The application does not silently overwrite another person's work or an approved result.

steps.action: After successful synchronization, inspect the relevant Workbench or intake receipt and resulting task state.
steps.expected: A synchronized draft may still require recording or reviewer submission. Sync success and analytical approval remain separate.
